result.title: What Does the Model See? Representation Validity in Multimodal LLM-Based Video Analysis
result.summary: Multimodal large language models (MLLMs) allow social scientists to analyze video at scale, but researchers must decide which parts of a video to provide as input. We use the term representation validity to examine how text, audio, video, and combined inputs affect measurement and subsequent analysis. We compare input representations across six open-weight MLLMs and three human-annotated video datasets. No representation consistently performs best. On seven news-related constructs, native-video performance varies little across models (macro-F1 = .70-.77), while extracted-text performance ranges from .52 to .80. Three models perform better with text and three with video. Combining inputs rarely improves performance. Higher classification accuracy also does not reliably produce estimates closer to those based on human codes. The highest-F1 representation best reproduces human-coded regression coefficients in 17 of 42 comparisons. Even when each model uses its highest-F1 deployable representation, 45% of sample-prevalence estimates differ from the human-coded benchmark by more than ten percentage points. Input representation therefore requires validation for both the construct being measured and the quantity estimated from the resulting labels.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文比较文本、音频、视频及组合输入在六个开源多模态大模型和三个视频数据集上的测量表现，发现没有始终最优的输入表示，组合输入也鲜有提升，且分类准确率更高并不保证下游估计更接近人工编码。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「表示效度」框架及「准确率不等于下游结论可靠」的发现，可供核查 LVR 中视觉证据筛选是否保留任务必要信息、latent 收益能否传递到最终判断；但研究对象是输入模态与社会科学测量，而非内部推理状态。
